sentences.text: Brief facts of this case are that on 20.02.2017 at about 05:00 PM, duty Officer had telephonically informed from JPC hospital to PS Khajuri Khas that one Pinki w/o Kapil Dev had been got admitted by her husband in an unconscious state 8498/17 whereupon the doctor concerned had declared her dead.
The said information was reduced into writing vide DD no. 70-B (Ex.PW15/A) and the same was marked to SI Satyadev (hereinafter referred to as Investigating Officer/IO).

Thereafter, IO along with Ct. Neeshu reached at JPC hospital and collected MLC of the deceased wherein the doctor State vs Kapil Dev on 3 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/133708082/
1 concerned had endorsed "alleged A/H/O being brought unconscious to the hospital with H/O hanging on 20.02.2017 at approximate one  hour back"
and "patient brought and declared dead.
Upon inquiry, the IO came to know that the deceased got married about one and  years ago.
The father of the deceased and SDM concerned were intimated.
The dead body of the deceased was got preserved at mortuary of GTB hospital through Ct. Neeshu.
IO visited the spot along with accused-husband Kapil Dev i.e. H.No. C-350, Gali No. 2, West Karawal Nagar.
The spot was got inspected through Crime team.
Photographs were taken from all angles.
One latch of the door was found to be forcefully broken from inside.
On the first floor of the above-stated house, one printed color saree which was torn into two piece was found lying which was seized vide seizure memo Ex. PW15/B.
On the next day, on 21.02.2017 the parents of the deceased reached at PS, who were taken to SDM office where SDM Sh. Daniel Masih recorded their statements.
Father of the deceased namely Jagpravesh had stated that he got his daughter married with Kapil Dev as per Hindu Rites and Ceremony about 1  year ago.
After about one month of the marriage, her in-laws started committing torture upon her, they used to beat her and used to make demand for dowry.
About 05:00 PM, day before, his daughter Pinki telephonically called him and stated that her in-laws are committing torture upon her and she requested to take her from there.
She also stated that the in-laws have also made her to starve.
On the basis of said statement of father of deceased, present FIR came to be registered.
After getting the dead body of deceased identified through her relatives, postmortem report of the deceased was got conducted at mortuary of GTB hospital.
In postmortem report Ex. PW1/E
, the cause of death was opined as "Asphyxia as a result of antemortem hanging".
Accused Kapil was arrested after interrogation and produced in the concerned court.
Since accused Mamchand had secured anticipatory bail, he was formally arrested.
After completion of of necessary formalities, charge-sheet was initially filed against the accused Kapil and Mamchand for offences punishable U/s 498A, 304B, 34 IPC.
Thereafter, CDR of mobile phone of accused Kranti was obtained.
As per which the location of mobile phone was located at some place in Rajasthan.
Meanwhile, viscera examination of report was also received.
On 02.07.2018, a supplementary charge-sheet was filed against Kranti and Kavita without arresting them.
COMMITTAL 2.
After taking cognizance and compliance of section 207 of IPC, the present case was committed to the court of Sessions.

The then Ld. District and Sessions judge allocated the present case to Ld.
Predecessor of this Court vide order dated 05.08.2017.

After hearing arguments and on finding that prima facie case was made out against the accused persons for the offence punishable u/s 498A/304B/34 of IPC, charges were framed by the ld.

sentences.text: Before examination of the evidence, oral and documentary, it would be appropriate to have a glance at relevant statutory provision and case law.

Section 304-B IPC defines 'dowry death', as under:
"(1) Where the death of a woman is caused by any burns or bodily injury or occurs otherwise than under normal circumstances within seven years of her marriage and it is shown that soon before her death she was subjected to cruelty or harassment by her husband or any relative of her husband for, or in connection with, any demand for dowry, such death shall be called "dowry death", and such husband or relative shall be deemed to have caused her death.
Explanation- For the purpose of this sub-section, "dowry" shall have the same meaning as in section 2 of the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961 (28 of 1961).
(2) Whoever commits dowry death shall be punished with imprisonment for a term which shall not be less than seven years but which may extend to imprisonment for life."

- When the question is whether a person has committed the dowry death of a women and it is shown that soon before her death such woman has been subjected by such person to cruelty or harassment for, or in connection with, any demand for dowry, the Court shall presume that such person had caused the dowry death.

sentences.text: The prosecution has to rule out the possibility of a natural or accidental death so as to bring it within the purview of "death occurring otherwise than in normal circumstances".
The expression "soon before" is very relevant where Section 113-B of the Evidence Act and Section 304- B IPC are pressed into service.
The prosecution is obliged to show that soon before the occurrence there was cruelty or harassment and only in that case presumption operates.
Evidence in that regard has to be led by the prosecution.

"Soon before" is a relative term and it would depend upon the circumstances of each case and no strait-jacket formula can be laid down as to what would constitute a period of soon before the occurrence.

It would be hazardous to indicate any fixed period, and that brings in the importance of a proximity test both for the proof of an offence of dowry death as well as for raising a presumption under Section 113-B of the Evidence Act.
The expression "soon before her death" used in the substantive Section 304-B IPC and Section 113-B of the Evidence Act is present with the idea of proximity test.
No definite period has been indicated and the expression "soon before" is not defined.

sentences.text: It was held therein that the inquest is not the substantive piece of evidence and can only be looked into for testing the veracity of the witnesses of inquest.

The crucial question is whether "soon before her death", the deceased was subjected to cruelty of harassment by the accused persons and such cruelty or harassment was in connection with demand for dowry.

17. In this regard, the material prosecution witnesses are PW3 Jagvansh (the father of the deceased),
PW4 Smt. Rajesh (the mother of the deceased), PW5 Kamal (uncle of the deceased), PW6 Nepal Singh (uncle of the deceased) and PW7 Satpal (uncle of the deceased).
On the basis of statement Ex.PW2/A and Ex.PW2/B recorded before Executive Magistrate Sh. Daniel Masih, the present FIR was registered.
In their statement, PW3 and PW4 had stated that the in-laws of their daughter Pinki had started harassing her after about one month of her marriage.
PW2 Jagvansh had claimed that about one week prior to the incident, he received a phone call of his deceased daughter wherein she had reported about torture committed upon her by her in-laws.
PW4 Smt. Rajesh had stated that her daughter was being harassed by her in-laws on account of non-meeting of their demand of dowry in the form of four wheeled vehicle by them.

However, in their depositions before the court,
all the family members of the deceased have taken a contrary stand.

Not only they have denied the suggestions put by Ld. Addl. PP for State based on their respective statements recorded during investigation, rather they had given clean chit to the accused persons in their respective examination-in-chiefs.

PW3 Jagvansh in his examination-in-chief dated 10.07.2018 had categorically testified that accused had never made any demand for him or his daughter had not made any complaint to him that she was harassed by her husband for demand of dowry.

They were nervous and perplexed condition and police obtained their thumb impression on the already written documents and SDM had made inquiry from him and his wife and he had disclosed name of his daughter and other particulars to the SDM.

Similarly, PW4 Smt. Rajesh in her examination-in-chief State vs Kapil Dev on 3 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/133708082/
15 dated 10.07.2018 too testified that she did not visit the matrimonial house of her daughter.
She did not make any complaint to her against her husband and in- laws.
PW5 Kamal in his examination-in-chief dated 10.07.2018 had also testified that there was no demand on the day of marriage.
PW6 Nepal Singh in his examination-in-chief dated 15.10.2018 categorically deposed that the deceased did not make any complaint to him against the accused persons during her marriage life.
PW7 Satpal in his examination-in-chief dated 15.10.2018 categorically testified that the deceased did not make any complaint to him against the accused persons during her marriage life.

18. It is well settled that the statements of the witnesses recorded during inquest proceedings can only be used for the purpose of corroboration, and substantive evidence is the testimony of witnesses recorded in the court.
In the present case, none of the family members of deceased had deposed that the deceased was subjected to cruelty or harassment at any point of time during her stay in the matrimonial house.

19. On careful analysis of evidence, it is apparent that there is no evidence of demand of dowry or subjecting the deceased to cruelty or harassment "soon before her death", for or in connection with dowry.
20. Presumption under Section 113-B of the Indian Evidence Act can be drawn only when prosecution first establishes essential ingredients Section 304-B of IPC.
Since the prosecution evidence could not prove essential ingredients of Section 304-B of IPC, the question of drawing presumption against the accused under Section 113-B of IPC does not arise.
Therefore, the prosecution has failed to prove the charge punishable under Section 304-B of IPC.
21. Perusal of postmortem report Ex.PW1/A would show that it was a case of suicide by hanging.
According to postmortem report, the cause of death was asphyxia as a result of ante- mortem hanging.
A reddish abraded dry hard ligature mark present incompletely and obliquely above the thyroid cartilage.
PW1 Dr. Vishwajeet Singh did not give any definite opinion as to whether the hanging was suicidal, homicidal or accidental.
Apart from the above-stated ligature mark, five more external injury marks have been reported in the PM report.

However, IO had not sought any subsequent opinion from the autopsy surgeon during investigation of the present case as to whether five external other injury marks as reported in the PM report are also sufficient to cause death of the deceased or not.
No question was put to the autopsy surgeon to ascertain whether it was a case of murder or suicidal death during his examination-in-chief dated 05.01.2018 and 23.02.2018.
There is no evidence to show that it was not a case of suicidal hanging.
From the pattern of ligature mark around the neck of the deceased, it can be safely concluded that it was a case of suicide by hanging.
Nor there is any evidence to indicate that the deceased wife was ever subjected to cruelty by the accused persons at any point of time prior to the date of incident.
